training_rows.design: direct multi-horizon: one row per (series, origin o, horizon h=1..19), target = Demand at o+h
training_rows.origins: every 2 months from 2020-01; only rows with target month <= cutoff
training_rows.filters: Train_Weight > 0 (excludes one-offs, measured events, gaps) and a defined scale (mean of last 12 > 0.1)

centred_anomaly_window.what: one-off orders are detected with a centred +-6 month median, so a flag in the last 6 months before a cutoff used up to 6 months of later data; flagged months are dropped from training targets

allocation_uplift_post_window_data.what: the difference-in-differences uplift for unlisted chip-shortage months uses up to 24 months after the window (to 2024-09); cutoffs 2023-10 and 2024-04 therefore saw a slightly better-informed history
allocation_uplift_post_window_data.affects: history from 2021-03 to 2022-09 only (>= 13 months before the earliest cutoff)

event_exclusion_decided_on_full_history.what: the list of material events (COVID, Nexon strike, 2022 price announcement) comes from the full history; the Nexon strike (2023-10/11) sits at the 2023-10 cutoff

macro_perfect_foresight.what: backtests use the realised macro value for the target month; in production the file supplies forecasts
macro_perfect_foresight.severity: unknown until measured -> experiment `no_macro` quantifies the dependence

tuning_on_backtest_folds.what: 5 parameter variants were compared on cutoffs 2024-04 and 2025-03; the defaults won
tuning_on_backtest_folds.severity: low (defaults kept, tiny search) -> the 6-cutoff evaluation adds 2 untouched cutoffs

intervals.sku_level: split-conformal: quantiles of actual/forecast by forecast-size bin x horizon bucket, from out-of-sample backtest forecasts; held-out coverage 80-83%
intervals.aggregate_level: log-normal error model per level: within-period noise + period shift with t-correction; held-out coverage 83-87%
